quote: This check tries to determine if the project has published a security policy.
stated_risk: Medium: possible insecure reporting of vulnerabilities

quote: This check tries to determine if the project has published a license.
stated_risk: Low: possible impediment to security review

quote: This check determines whether the project has generated executable (binary) artifacts in the source repository.
stated_risk: High: non-reviewable code

quote: This check determines whether the project's GitHub Action workflows has dangerous code patterns.
stated_risk: Critical: vulnerable to repository compromise

quote: This check determines whether the project's automated workflows tokens follow the principle of least privilege.
stated_risk: High: vulnerable to malicious code additions

quote: This check tries to determine if the project pins dependencies used during its build and release process.
stated_risk: Medium: possible compromised dependencies

quote: This check tries to determine if the project uses a dependency update tool, specifically one of: - Dependabot - Renovate bot Out-of-date dependencies make a project vulnerable to known flaws and prone to attacks.
stated_risk: High: possibly vulnerable to attacks on known flaws

quote: This check tries to determine if the project is published as a package.
stated_risk: Medium: users possibly missing security updates

quote: This check determines whether the project requires human code review before pull requests (merge requests) are merged.
stated_risk: High: unintentional vulnerabilities or possible injection of malicious code

quote: This check tries to determine if the project cryptographically signs release artifacts.
stated_risk: High: possibility of installing malicious releases

quote: This check determines whether the project has open, unfixed vulnerabilities in its own codebase or its dependencies using the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) service.
stated_risk: High: known vulnerabilities

quote: This check tries to determine if the project uses fuzzing by checking: 1. if the repository name is included in the OSS-Fuzz project list; 2. if ClusterFuzzLite is deployed in the repository; 3. if there are user-defined language-specified fuzzing functions in the repository. - currently only supports Go fuzzing, - a limited set of property-based testing libraries for Haskell including QuickCheck, Hedgehog, validity or SmallCheck, - a limited set of property-based testing libraries for JavaScript and TypeScript including fast-check. - a limited set of property-based testing libraries for Erlang, including proper and quickcheck. - a limited set of property-based testing libraries for C# and F# including FsCheck.
stated_risk: Medium: possible vulnerabilities in code

quote: This check determines whether a project's default and release branches are protected with GitHub's branch protection or repository rules settings.
stated_risk: High: vulnerable to intentional malicious code injection

quote: This check tries to determine if the project has recent contributors from multiple organizations (e.g., companies).
stated_risk: Low: lower number of trusted code reviewers

quote: This check determines whether the webhook defined in the repository has a token configured to authenticate the origins of requests. **Remediation steps** - Check if the service your webhooks is configured with supports secrets. - If there is support for token authentication, set the secret in the webhook configuration.
stated_risk: Critical: service possibly accessible to third parties

quote: This check tries to determine if the project runs tests before pull requests are merged.
stated_risk: Low: possible unknown vulnerabilities

quote: This check tries to determine if the project uses Static Application Security Testing (SAST), also known as static code analysis.
stated_risk: Medium: possible unknown bugs

quote: This check determines whether the project has earned an OpenSSF (formerly CII) Best Practices Badge at the passing, silver, or gold level.
stated_risk: Low: possibly not following security best practices

quote: This check tries to determine if the project maintains a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) either as a file in the source or a release artifact.
stated_risk: Medium: possible inaccurate reporting of dependencies/vulnerabilities
